findings.description: Spec text says 'GOOGLEFINANCE's trade date' without naming the attribute. Real code uses GOOGLEFINANCE("{ticker}","tradetime") in sheets-view/lib.rs:270. A1 invents 'price' (wrong), A2 invents 'date' (wrong), A3 omits GOOGLEFINANCE entirely (wrong). All B-outputs correctly identify 'tradetime' as the attribute.
findings.failure_scenario: Spec reader has no way to know GOOGLEFINANCE exposes a 'tradetime' attribute; A-outputs all guess differently and incorrectly. Code enforces 'tradetime'; B-outputs all infer it correctly from the formula.

findings.short_summary: Date truncation uses INT(), not DAYS() or direct subtraction
findings.description: Spec says 'integer count of days since 1970-01-01' without specifying the calculation method. Real code uses INT(GOOGLEFINANCE(...,"tradetime")) in sheets-view/lib.rs:271. A1 uses DAYS(...,DATE(1970,1,1)), A2 uses GOOGLEFINANCE(...)-DATE(...), A3 uses TODAY()-DATE(...). All B-outputs correctly identify INT() as the truncation method.
findings.failure_scenario: A-outputs invent three different formulas to achieve 'integer count of days'; none match the real code's INT() truncation. B-outputs all converge on INT() by reading the code directly.

findings.short_summary: Default value on parse failure is 0 (epoch anchor), not error or None
findings.description: Spec text does not specify fallback behavior for unparseable/empty cells. Real code (runtime/adapters.rs:316-319) uses .unwrap_or(0) to default to epoch date on parse failure. A-outputs do not address parsing semantics. B-outputs all identify the 0-default as the settle-pass tie-break for empty/invalid quote-date cells.
findings.failure_scenario: A-outputs focus on formula generation; B-outputs add specification of the read-back parser's null-handling (0-default), which the spec does not pin.
